source_text: νόμον, οἱ τὰ ὀρθῶς ἔχοντα διαστρέφοντες αἱρετικοὶ καταθύουσι γὰρ τὸν ἀμνὸν, οὐκ ἐν τῇ ἁγίᾳ πόλει, οὔτε μὴν διὰ χειρὸς τῶν ἐξειλεγμένων διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος εἰς ἱερουργίαν, ἀλλ' ὡς ὁ θεῖος ἡμῖν γράφει Παῦλος, ἑαυτοῖς ἁρπάζοντες τὴν τιμὴν, καὶ ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ προσάγοντες. Ταῦροι γὰρ ὥσπερ ὑβρισταὶ καὶ ἀγέρωχοι, πρὸς μόνον ἀδιακρίτως ἴενται τὸ σφίσι δοκοῦν. Ἀλλ' ἐκεῖνοι μὲν πολὺ τὸ ἐξήνιον καὶ τὸ νενευκὸς εἰς ἀπόνοιαν ἐπιτηδεύοντες, πικρὰ τῷ κριτῇ τῶν τοιῶνδε διασκεμμάτων τίσουσι δίκας. Ἴωμεν δὲ πάλιν ἡμεῖς εἰς οἶμον τὴν ἐντριβῆ τε καὶ ἀδιάστροφον, ἐκεῖνο τοῦ παρενηνεγμένου δοκιμάζοντες νόμου. Διεπύθου γάρ που λέγοντος σαφῶς, ὅτι «Φυλάξατε τὸν μῆνα τῶν νέων, καὶ ποιήσεις τὸ Πάσχα Κυρίῳ τῷ Θεῷ σου, πρόβατα καὶ βόας.» Καί τοι τί δή ποτε, φαίη τις ἂν, τὸν ἐπὶ τῷ Πάσχα νόμον τοῖς ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ τιθεὶς, ἕνα μόνον ἐκέλευσε καταθύειν ἀμνόν· προβάτων δὲ καὶ μόσχων μεμνημένον οὐχ εὑρήσομεν; Ἆρ' οὖν τοῦ πρέποντος διημάρτηκεν ὁ Μωσῆς; Οὐδαμῶς· ἐν γάρ τοι τοῖς Ἀριθμοῖς προσεπάγεσθαι τῷ ἀμνῷ βοῦς τε καὶ ὄεις ἐπενομοθέτει Θεὸς οὕτω λέγων· «Καὶ ἐν τῷ μηνὶ τῷ πρώτῳ τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ μηνὸς Πάσχα τῷ Κυρίῳ, καὶ τῇ πεντεκαιδεκάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ μηνὸς τούτου ἑορτὴ, ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας ἄζυμα ἔδεσθε, καὶ ἡμέρα ἡ πρώτη ἐπίκλητος ἁγία ἔσται ὑμῖν, πᾶν ἔργον λατρευτὸν οὐ ποιήσετε. Καὶ προσάξετε ὁλοκαυτώματα κάρπωμα Κυρίῳ, μόσχους ἐκ βοῶν δύο, κριὸν ἕνα, ἀμνοὺς ἐνιαυσίους ἑπτὰ, ἄμωμοι ἔσονται ὑμῖν, καὶ θυσία αὐτῶν σεμίδαλις ἀναπεποιημένη ἐν ἐλαίῳ, τρία δέκατα τῷ μόσχῳ τῷ ἑνὶ, καὶ δύο δέκατα τῷ κριῷ τῷ ἑνί. Δέκατον δέκατον ποιήσεις τῷ ἀμνῷ τῷ ἑνὶ, τοῖς ἑπτὰ ἀμνοῖς, καὶ χίμαρον ἐξ αἰγῶν ἕνα περὶ ἁμαρτίας, ἐξιλάσασθαι περὶ ὑμῶν. Πλὴν τῆς ὁλοκαυτώσεως τῆς διαπαντὸς τῆς πρωϊνῆς, ὅ ἐστιν ὁλοκαύτωμα ἐνδελεχισμοῦ. Ταῦτα κατὰ ταῦτα ποιήσετε τὴν ἡμέραν εἰς τὰς ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας, δῶρον κάρπωμα εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας Κυρίῳ ἐπὶ τοῦ ὁλοκαυτώματος τοῦ διαπαντὸς, ποιήσεις τὴν σπονδὴν αὐτοῦ. Καὶ ἡμέρα ἡ ἑβδόμη κλητὴ ἁγία ἔσται ὑμῖν, πᾶν ἔργον λατρευτὸν οὐ ποιήσετε ἐν αὐτῇ.» Ὅτι μὲν οὖν ἐν μηνὶ τῷ πρώτῳ, καὶ μέντοι καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτῃ τὸ Πάσχα πληροῦν ἀνάγκη κατὰ τὸν νόμον, φθάσαντες ἤδη προείπομεν. Τί δ' ἂν βούλοιτο δηλοῦν καὶ τῶν ἀζύμων ἡ βρῶσις, καὶ ἡ κατὰ Σάββατον ἀργία, καὶ πρὸς τούτοις ἔτι τὸ ὠνομάσθαι κλητὰς ἁγίας τήν τε πρώτην καὶ τὴν ἑβδόμην ἡμέραν, προαπέδειξε σαφῶς ὁ λόγος. Τοιγάρτοι μεθεὶς τὸ ἔν γε τουτοισὶ διαμέλλειν ἔτι, ἐπὶ τοὺς τῶν θυσιῶν πάλιν ἴωμεν τρόπους. Δύο μὲν τοίνυν οἱ μόσχοι, πρὸς ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ θυσίαν, εἷς δὲ κριὸς, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἀμνοὶ τὸν ἀριθμὸν ἑπτὰ, πάντες ἄμωμοί τε καὶ ἐνιαύσιοι, καὶ θυσία μὲν ἐπ' αὐτοῖς, σεμίδαλις ἐλαιόδευτος. Πλὴν οὐκ ἐν ἴσῳ μέτρῳ· τρία μὲν γὰρ ἑκάστῳ μόσχῳ δέκατα, δύο δὲ τῷ κριῷ, καὶ ἓν ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ τῶν ἀμνῶν. Εἶτα συνεισφέρεται καὶ χίμαρος ἐξ αἰγῶν, ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτίας· «Καὶ ταυτὶ δὴ πάντα,» φησὶ,
pass_a_gloss: (Through nothing then do they make the) law about this, the heretics twisting the things that are right; for they sacrifice the lamb not in the holy city, nor indeed through the hand of those chosen through the Spirit for sacred service, but, as divine Paul writes to us, snatching for themselves the honor, and bringing (offerings) in every place. For like bulls insolent and haughty, they rush indiscriminately toward only what seems (good) to them. But those, practicing much the unbridled and the leaning into madness, will pay bitter penalties to the judge of such deliberations. And let us go again ourselves into the trodden and undistorted path, testing that (point) of the law brought forward. For you heard somewhere (it) saying clearly that: Guard the month of the new (things), and you will make the Passover to the Lord your God, sheep and oxen. And yet why ever, someone might say, setting the law about the Passover for those in Egypt, did he command to sacrifice one lamb only, and we will not find (him) having mentioned sheep and calves? Did Moses then miss the fitting? Not at all; for in the Numbers God further legislated that oxen and sheep be brought in addition to the lamb, saying thus: And in the first month on the fourteenth day of the month (is) Passover to the Lord, and on the fifteenth day of this month a feast, seven days you will eat unleavened (breads), and the first day will be for you called holy, every servile work you will not do. And you will bring whole burnt offerings, a fruit-offering to the Lord, calves from oxen two, ram one, lambs of a year seven, they will be blameless for you, and their sacrifice fine flour worked up in oil, three tenths to the one calf, and two tenths to the one ram. A tenth a tenth you will make to the one lamb, for the seven lambs, and one goat from goats concerning sin, to propitiate concerning you. Besides the whole burnt offering, the continual one of the morning, which is a whole burnt offering of continuance. These according to these you will do the day for the seven days, a gift fruit-offering for an odor of fragrance to the Lord upon the whole burnt offering of the continual; you will make its libation. And the seventh day will be for you called holy, every servile work you will not do in it. That then in the first month, and moreover on the fourteenth day, it is necessary to fulfill the Passover according to the law, having anticipated we already said before. And what would wish to show both the eating of the unleavened (breads), and the idleness according to sabbath, and in addition to these the having been named called-holy both the first and the seventh day, the argument showed clearly before. So, letting go the still lingering in these, let us go again to the manners of the sacrifices. Two then the calves, for whole burnt offerings and sacrifice, and one ram, and indeed lambs in number seven, all blameless and yearly, and sacrifice upon them, fine flour oil-moistened; except not in equal measure: for three tenths to each calf, two to the ram, and one upon each of the lambs. Then a goat from goats is brought in together, on behalf of sin: And all these, he says, (continues).
pass_b_english: Cyril: … law on this point, those heretics who twist what is right. For they sacrifice the lamb not in the holy city, nor by the hands of those chosen through the Spirit for sacred service, but, as the divine Paul writes to us, they seize the honor for themselves (Hebrews 5:4) and offer in every place. Like insolent and unruly bulls they charge without discernment at whatever alone seems good to them. But they, practicing so much unbridled license and a bent toward madness, will pay a bitter penalty to the judge of such schemes. Let us go back again to the well-worn and straight path, and examine this point in the law that was cited. You heard it say clearly, ‘Observe the month of the new crops, and you shall keep the Passover to the Lord your God, sheep and oxen’ (Deuteronomy 16:1–2). And yet why, someone might say, when he laid down the law of the Passover for those in Egypt, did he command only one lamb to be sacrificed, while we shall not find him mentioning sheep and calves? Did Moses, then, miss what was fitting? Not at all. For in Numbers God made a further law, that oxen and sheep be brought in addition to the lamb, saying, ‘And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is the Passover to the Lord. And on the fifteenth day of this month is a feast; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread. And the first day shall be called holy for you; you shall do no servile work. And you shall offer whole burnt offerings, an offering by fire to the Lord: two calves from the herd, one ram, seven lambs a year old; they shall be without blemish for you. And their sacrifice shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for the one calf, and two tenths for the one ram. You shall make a tenth, a tenth for each lamb, for the seven lambs; and one male goat for sin, to make propitiation for you; besides the continual whole burnt offering of the morning, which is a whole burnt offering of perpetuity. In this way you shall make these each day for the seven days, a gift, an offering by fire for a fragrant aroma to the Lord; besides the continual whole burnt offering you shall make its drink offering. And the seventh day shall be called holy for you; you shall do no servile work on it’ (Numbers 28:16–25).

That the Passover must be kept, according to the law, in the first month, and on the fourteenth day, we have already said earlier. And what the eating of unleavened bread would mean, and the rest on the sabbath, and besides that the naming of both the first day and the seventh as ‘called holy’, our discussion has already shown clearly. So, ceasing to linger any longer over these, let us go once more to the manners of the sacrifices. There are, then, two calves for whole burnt offerings and sacrifice, one ram, and lambs to the number of seven, all without blemish and a year old; and the sacrifice with them is fine flour mixed with oil, but not in equal measure: three tenths for each calf, two for the ram, and one for each of the lambs. Then a male goat is brought in with them for sin. ‘And all these,’ it says,…

choices.english: they seize the honor for themselves (Hebrews 5:4)
choices.why: Cyril’s turn of Hebrews 5:4 (‘no one takes this honor for himself’).

choices.english: their sacrifice shall be fine flour
choices.why: In Numbers θυσία is the grain offering; ‘sacrifice’ is kept because Cyril pairs ‘whole burnt offerings and sacrifice’.
The continual daily offering; Cyril names it ‘of perpetuity’ again in §16.
